flavor: Where the fire under the world breaks through. Some of them are only sleeping.
rules: Any named volcano, active, dormant or long extinct, on land, under the sea or on another world. Saying 'Mount' or 'Volcano' is optional. A mountain that was never a volcano doesn't count.

answers.lore: It buried Pompeii and Herculaneum in AD 79. It last erupted in 1944.
The tallest active volcano in Europe outside the Caucasus, and one of the busiest on Earth.
It last erupted in 1707, and pilgrims have climbed it for centuries.
Its 1883 eruption was heard nearly 5,000 km away, perhaps the loudest sound in recorded history.
Its 1980 eruption tore about 400 m off the top of the mountain.
Africa's highest mountain, and a dormant volcano.
A supervolcano beneath the world's first national park, founded in 1872.
Its ash closed much of Europe's airspace for days in April 2010.
Erupting almost without pause for over 2,000 years, it is called the Lighthouse of the Mediterranean.
The largest active volcano on Earth by volume.
Hawaiian tradition says the goddess Pele makes her home in its crater.
Its 1991 eruption cooled the whole planet by about half a degree for a year or so.
Its name means 'smoking mountain' in Nahuatl.
Its Bronze Age eruption may have helped bring down the Minoans, and is sometimes linked to Atlantis.
Spain's highest mountain, on Tenerife.
A volcano on Mars about two and a half times the height of Everest.
Measured from its base on the sea floor, it is taller than Everest.
Its 1815 eruption, the largest in recorded history, brought the Year Without a Summer in 1816.
In medieval Europe it was said to be a gateway to hell.
Its 1902 eruption destroyed the town of Saint-Pierre in minutes, killing almost everyone in it.
The southernmost active volcano on Earth, with a lake of lava in its crater.
A dormant volcano, where legend says Noah's Ark came to rest.
A dormant volcano, and the highest mountain in Europe by most counts.
A 2025 law made it and its neighbouring peaks a legal person. Its official name is now Taranaki Maunga.
Also called White Island. Its 2019 eruption killed 22 people visiting the crater.
Its 2022 eruption was the largest explosion in the atmosphere ever recorded by modern instruments.
Home to one of the largest lava lakes on Earth.
Its 1783 eruption poisoned Iceland's livestock, and the famine that followed killed about a fifth of its people.
An island born from the sea in 1963, kept almost untouched so scientists can watch life arrive.
The island that gave every volcano its name, after Vulcan, the Roman god of fire.
A vast caldera under the suburbs of Naples, where the ground rises and falls by metres.
Its 2021 eruption on La Palma lasted 85 days and buried whole villages.
Born in a Mexican cornfield in 1943, it grew more than 300 m in its first year.
Its 1985 eruption sent mudflows that buried the town of Armero.
Its summit is the farthest point on Earth from the planet's centre.
Its collapse about 7,700 years ago left the basin that now holds Crater Lake.
Its name means 'house of the sun'.
Named by British sailors who mistook the calcite crystals on its slopes for diamonds.
Its eruption about 74,000 years ago was one of the largest of the last two million years.
An extinct volcano in the middle of Edinburgh.
Its name means 'child of Krakatoa'. It rose from the sea in 1927.
Its famous crater, crowded with wildlife, is the caldera of a great volcano that collapsed millions of years ago.
Spanish friars called it the mouth of hell, and planted a cross on its rim to keep the devil in.
The highest volcano on Earth, on the border of Chile and Argentina.
Three Inca children, sacrificed some 500 years ago, were found near its summit in 1999.
Where Jules Verne's travellers set off on their Journey to the Centre of the Earth.
Its eruptions of 1730 to 1736 buried about a quarter of Lanzarote.
Portugal's highest mountain, on an island in the Azores.
Blaise Pascal's brother-in-law carried a barometer up it in 1648 to show that air pressure falls with height.
It played Mount Doom in The Lord of the Rings films.
Its 1886 eruption destroyed the Pink and White Terraces, once called the eighth wonder of the world.
Auckland's youngest volcano, risen from the sea about 600 years ago.
Its glow drew Captain Cook ashore in 1774, and it has hardly stopped erupting since.
Famous for blue flames, from sulphur gas burning as it leaves the ground.
The legendary birthplace of the Korean people, and the site of a huge eruption around AD 946.
Its name means 'smoking mountain' in the Afar language, and it held a lava lake for decades.
A flooded caldera in Antarctica, where ships sail right into the crater.
Born in about a week in 1538, it is one of the youngest mountains in Europe.
The largest volcano in Europe, hidden under the Tyrrhenian Sea.
Its 1600 eruption, the largest in South America's recorded history, may have caused a famine in Russia.
With its neighbour Vulcan, it erupted in 1994 and buried much of the town of Rabaul in ash.
Sumatra's most active volcano, not to be confused with Java's Merapi. Its eruption in December 2023 killed 24 climbers.
Its three crater lakes are different colours, and every so often they change.
A mountain on Saturn's moon Titan, thought to be an ice volcano, and named after Tolkien's Mount Doom.
Its eruption on 23 November 2025 was the first ever recorded. The ash cloud drifted as far as India and China.
An undersea volcano where sharks were found living inside the crater, which earned it the name Sharkcano.
Not the clock. A volcano on Australia's Heard Island, and taller than any mountain on the Australian mainland.
A cone in the Rabaul caldera in Papua New Guinea. It formed in 1878 and erupted again in 1937 and in 1994, alongside Tavurvur.
Britain's highest mountain is all that remains of a volcano that died out in the Devonian period, long before the dinosaurs.
Erupted in August 2025, days after a magnitude 8.8 earthquake off Kamchatka, for the first time in centuries.
In 1982 its ash stopped all four engines of a British Airways jumbo jet. The crew glided out of the cloud, restarted them and landed safely.
A study in 2020 linked its great eruption of 43 BC to the cold, hungry years after Julius Caesar's murder.
In 1986 a cloud of carbon dioxide burst from the lake in its crater and smothered about 1,700 people.
On 1 April 1974 a prankster set a pile of old tyres alight in its crater, and the people of Sitka thought it was erupting.
In the novel Picnic at Hanging Rock, schoolgirls vanish here in 1900. The story is fiction, though many readers believed it.
A cluster of volcanic domes on the Moon. China's Chang'e 5 landed nearby in 2020 and brought rock back to Earth.
The only volcano known to erupt carbonatite lava in historical times. It flows black and cool, then turns white as snow.
Known until 2021 as Lōʻihi: the youngest volcano in the Hawaiian chain, its summit still about 975 m under the sea.
It rose off Sicily in 1831 and was claimed by Britain, France, Spain and the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies, then sank within months.
